# Rudis — Strategic Financing Term Sheet Framework

**Status:** non-binding negotiation framework for strategic financing / sponsored R&D / investment discussions.

It is not a securities offering, binding term sheet or legal advice.

## 1. Proposed transaction concept

Preferred first structure for a strategic partner such as Meta:

**Staged strategic R&D financing of up to USD 12,000,000**, followed by an **optional separately approved program of up to USD 15,000,000** if technical and commercial gates are met.

No automatic D3, D4 or production authorization follows from financing.

## 2. Indicative stages

### Phase I — Diligence / convergence / independent validation

Indicative envelope: **USD 1.5M**.

Objectives:

- legal / IP diligence;
- one converged PRE-D3 candidate;
- reproducibility and independent review;
- security hardening;
- partner-specific opportunity / threat model;
- technical evaluation package.

### Phase II — Controlled D3 laboratory

Indicative envelope: **USD 4.5M**.

Begins only if D3 readiness and the required Rudis authorization are separately achieved.

Objectives:

- multi-client controlled environment;
- recovery / replay / concurrency / stale-state attacks;
- independent security review;
- agent / tool-use integration;
- synthetic/internal users only;
- no real money / production by default.

### Phase III — Strategic reference integration

Indicative envelope: **USD 6M**.

Objectives:

- selected partner reference integration;
- AI-agent authority gateway and/or immersive/wearable client;
- production-readiness research without automatic production authorization;
- commercialization / licensing analysis.

### Optional Phase IV — controlled field program

Up to **USD 15M additional**, only by separate agreement.

## 3. Founder autonomy economics

### A. Founder Strategic Reserve

Preferred negotiation position:

**not less than 10% of each funded tranche** is allocated to the Founder Strategic Reserve.

The founder may deploy this reserve without transaction-level investor approval for lawful project, strategic, research, hiring, tooling, travel, advisory, contingency, ecosystem or opportunity purposes reasonably related to Rudis / Quebranto activities.

Accounting and aggregate reporting remain applicable.

### B. Founder Liquidity / Compensation

A separate founder-liquidity mechanism should be negotiated outside ordinary project OPEX.

Possible structures, subject to legal/tax advice:

- salary / management compensation;
- transaction or signing consideration where lawful;
- founder bonus;
- reimbursement of valid historic expenditures;
- limited secondary transaction after a suitable corporate structure exists;
- licensing consideration for founder-held IP where appropriate.

The objective is to provide legitimate founder personal liquidity without disguising personal funds as project expenditure.

## 4. Use of funds — indicative model

Each phase may include:

- engineering / research;
- security and independent audit;
- infrastructure / compute;
- legal / IP / compliance;
- integration / productization;
- contractors / specialist hiring;
- business development;
- founder compensation;
- Founder Strategic Reserve (>=10% target);
- contingency.

Precise budget categories may be rebalanced by management within an agreed variance band without investor preapproval.

Recommended management flexibility:

- up to 20% reallocation between ordinary budget categories without consent;
- Founder Strategic Reserve controlled according to its own rule;
- material change of total program scope may require partner consultation.

## 5. Economic rights a strategic partner may reasonably request

Depending on structure:

- milestone reporting;
- financial reporting on funded program;
- defined audit rights;
- access to agreed diligence materials;
- internal evaluation license;
- reference-integration rights;
- time-limited right of first negotiation for agreed commercial fields;
- option to negotiate commercial licenses to licensable private components;
- strategic investment rights in a future operating vehicle if separately agreed.

## 6. Rights not granted automatically

Financing alone does not grant:

- ownership of the Rudis Canon;
- control of the Assembly;
- constitutional authority;
- the Red Button;
- perpetual exclusivity;
- ownership of all present/future founder IP;
- unrestricted private-Forge access;
- rights to RU / reserves / monetary policy;
- production authorization;
- unilateral authority to expand D3/D4 scope;
- veto over unrelated founder projects.

## 7. Exclusivity

Preferred position: **no broad exclusivity**.

If requested:

- limited to a narrowly defined commercial field;
- limited in time;
- contingent on minimum funding / performance;
- separately compensated;
- terminates if partner stops funding or fails agreed milestones;
- does not restrict retained fields, open-source obligations or unrelated founder work.

A **Right of First Negotiation (ROFN)** is preferred over a broad Right of First Refusal (ROFR).

## 8. IP structure

Preferred principles:

- founder/project background IP remains with existing rightsholders unless specifically licensed or assigned;
- partner background IP remains partner-owned;
- foreground IP is allocated by a clear agreement;
- public AGPL code remains subject to AGPL;
- commercial rights should focus on services, private components, integration, support, infrastructure, brand/certification and lawfully licensable assets;
- no representation that all third-party/contributor rights are consolidated until diligence confirms it.

## 9. Governance / control

The contracting vehicle may have ordinary corporate governance appropriate to investment.

That governance must not be silently conflated with Rudis constitutional governance.

`COMPANY BOARD RIGHTS != RUDIS CANON AUTHORITY`

Investor reserved matters should be narrow and extraordinary.

## 10. Founder freedom

Preferred founder protections:

- freedom to continue unrelated research and projects;
- no blanket future-IP assignment;
- no perpetual personal exclusivity;
- no broad personal guarantees;
- no investor approval requirement for ordinary technical decisions;
- no automatic forfeiture of founder background IP on termination;
- reasonable cure periods before loss of material contractual rights;
- termination of unused exclusivity if funding ceases.

## 11. Milestone principle

Tranche release should be tied to demonstrable outcomes, not investor micromanagement.

```text
GATE / DELIVERABLE
-> EVIDENCE
-> REVIEW
-> RELEASE
```

A failed technical hypothesis may still count as valuable R&D output if the phase was expressly designed to falsify it; however, continuation funding may be stopped according to agreed gates.

## 12. Diligence conditions before binding close

At minimum:

- contracting vehicle / founder structure;
- IP chain-of-title review;
- contributor agreements where material;
- third-party license inventory;
- security/publication review;
- tax treatment;
- financial account / bookkeeping setup;
- sanctions / KYC / AML checks as legally applicable;
- data protection review for any shared personal/confidential data;
- definitive scope and milestones;
- definitive founder compensation / liquidity mechanism;
- definitive Founder Strategic Reserve language.

## 13. Negotiation walk-away triggers

Strongly reconsider a deal requiring:

- blanket all-IP assignment;
- perpetual worldwide exclusivity;
- personal control rights over the founder;
- partner authority over Rudis constitutional decisions;
- project-wide access unrelated to diligence;
- removal of founder discretion from ordinary operations;
- personal guarantees disproportionate to the transaction;
- funding terminable at will while partner retains permanent expansive rights;
- prohibition on unrelated future founder work;
- hidden conversion of R&D sponsorship into ownership of the entire ecosystem.

## 14. Closing principle

> The partner should receive a fair economic bargain, credible evidence and contractual protection. The founder should receive enough capital and personal freedom to build without becoming an employee of the financing agreement in everything but name.
